title: The norm of an ample invertible sheaf along a finite morphism with a degree d norm is ample on the base

standard_prerequisites.name: A scheme carrying an ample invertible sheaf is quasi-compact, and the existence of a norm of degree d implies that the morphism is surjective
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives quasi-compactness of the base, which is the first half of the ampleness criterion being applied.

standard_prerequisites.name: Ampleness tested by affine caps: it suffices to find, at every point, a section of a positive tensor power not vanishing at that point whose nonvanishing locus is affine, and the existence of a section of a high power of an ample sheaf whose nonvanishing locus separates a finite set from a prescribed affine open
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the section downstairs whose nonvanishing locus lies inside a chosen affine open and whose behaviour at the norm is controlled.

standard_prerequisites.name: The norm of a section: for a finite morphism with a degree d norm the norm of a section of a power of an invertible sheaf is a section of the same power of the norm, whose vanishing behaviour is controlled by the section's vanishing behaviour
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the candidate sheaf on the base as ample and gives the nonvanishing statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: The nonvanishing locus of a section of a sheaf restricted to an affine open is affine
standard_prerequisites.use: Concludes that the cap of the chosen section is affine, completing the ampleness criterion.

core_obligations: Set up the candidate: let the given ample invertible sheaf on the source be L and prove that its norm is ample on the base (proof lines 3744-3746).

Get quasi-compactness of the base: the source is quasi-compact because it carries an ample invertible sheaf, and the morphism is surjective because a norm exists, so the base is quasi-compact (proof lines 3748-3749).

Produce a section with an affine cap at an arbitrary point: choose an affine open neighbourhood of the point in the base, then choose a high power of the ample sheaf and a section whose nonvanishing locus contains the fibre over the point and is contained in the preimage of that affine open (proof lines 3750-3761).

Conclude ampleness: the norm of that section is a section of the corresponding power of the norm sheaf, it does not vanish at the point, and its nonvanishing locus lies inside the chosen affine open and is therefore affine, which is exactly the cap criterion for ampleness of the norm sheaf (proof lines 3762-3767).
proof_roadmap: Show the base is quasi-compact using ampleness on the source and surjectivity from the existence of a norm (proof lines 3748-3749).

At an arbitrary point pick a section of a high power with nonvanishing locus between the fibre and a chosen affine neighbourhood, take its norm, and read off the affine cap criterion (proof lines 3750-3767).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that if a finite morphism admits a norm of degree d and its source carries an ample invertible sheaf, then the base carries one too, namely the norm of that sheaf (statement lines 3737-3742). The counted proof is short but complete: it obtains quasi-compactness of the base from ampleness on the source and surjectivity of the morphism, then at an arbitrary point uses the ample sheaf to find a section of a high power whose nonvanishing locus sits between the fibre over the point and a chosen affine neighbourhood, takes its norm, and applies the cap criterion for ampleness using that the nonvanishing locus of a section inside an affine open is affine (proof lines 3744-3767). It is H2: the argument is carried out in the counted span and its inputs are the standard ampleness criterion and the properties of the norm map.
